109-1-LB101_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB101_Intro_Copy.docx LB101 amends Nebraska’s Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act to (1) affirm a tenant’s right to a jury trial and bar rental-agreement waivers of rights under state or federal law; (2) require complaints for restitution to be filed with the clerk of the district or county court and permit inclusion of a jury demand; (3) revise summons content and service rules (including a three‑day service window, five‑day return, and filer affidavit) to notify defendants of the right to a jury trial; and (4) impose specific duties on courts—informing defendants of jury rights, inquiring about jury demands in county court, scheduling jury trials as practicable, and allowing courts to require tenants to deposit accrued rent if a tenant-requested jury trial is continued. If judgment for possession is entered, the court issues writs of restitution directing the constable or sheriff to restore possession. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are made. Original cited sections are repealed. Adds procedural provisions for courts handling possession actions: complaints may include a jury demand and must notify defendants of their right to a jury trial. If a defendant has not demanded a jury by first appearance, the court must inform them and, in county court cases, ask whether they demand a jury or elect a bench trial. If tried by the court, the trial must occur 10–14 days after summons; if by jury, it must be scheduled as soon as practicable. If a tenant requests a continuance beyond the initial date, the court may require the tenant to deposit accruing rent with the clerk of court. No agencies beyond courts/county courts and the court clerk are created or given funding; no appropriations or budget changes are specified. DOCX | PDF

109-1-LB111_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB111_Intro_Copy.docx LB111 (Nebraska) regulates insurers' handling of motor-vehicle repairs. It defines insurer, consumer, consumer care, nonoriginal equipment manufacturer (non‑OEM) and part. Key provisions: insurers may not require non‑OEM parts that lack permanent manufacturer identification or that are inferior in fit/performance (costs to modify count toward quality). Insurers must obtain written consumer consent before using non‑OEM parts, may not charge consumers the price difference for choosing OEM parts, and must identify intended non‑OEM parts in estimates. A prescribed 10‑point notice must be provided before repairs. Insurers may not require aftermarket parts for vehicles manufactured within 36 months of damage; an optional policy notice is allowed for older vehicles. Violations are Class I misdemeanors. No state agencies, departments, or budget appropriations are referenced. Adds definitions (consumer, consumer care, insurer, nonoriginal equipment manufacturer, part) and imposes requirements on insurers handling motor-vehicle repairs: non‑OEM parts must carry permanent identification, be equal in fit/performance to OEM parts (including modification costs), be disclosed in estimates, and require written consumer consent before use; insurers cannot charge consumers the price difference for choosing OEM parts. Insurers must give a 10‑point type notice before repairs and may include a standard policy notice for older vehicles; insurers may not mandate aftermarket parts for vehicles under 36 months. Violations are a Class I misdemeanor. No government agencies or departments are named and there are no funding, appropriation, or budget changes. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB112_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB112_Intro_Copy.docx LB112 amends motor-vehicle salvage title law. Adds a definition cross-referencing "consumer care" to section 60‑1401.10 and specifies that a vehicle may be deemed "structurally totaled" by both a facility that performs consumer care and by the insurer that insured the vehicle when damage occurred. Defines "structurally totaled vehicle" as one totaled due to a kink or crease in a frame rail, unibody, or structural component (including engine cradle or rear differential). Excludes vehicles totaled solely for hail or cosmetic damage and those whose repair costs do not exceed 75% of actual cash value. 109-1-LB130_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB130_Intro_Copy.docx LB130 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §77-4602 to clarify monthly and annual reporting and to revise automatic transfers from the General Fund to the Cash Reserve Fund. The Tax Commissioner must publish monthly actual General Fund net receipts and comparisons to the Nebraska Economic Forecasting Advisory Board forecast and prior-year receipts, and a fiscal‑year summary comparing actual and certified estimated receipts (per §§77-4601 and 77-4603). Within 15 days after year-end the Tax Commissioner computes (a) the surplus (actual minus certified estimate) and (b) 50% of a growth-based formula; if the surplus is positive the greater amount is certified to the Director of Administrative Services. Upon that certification the State Treasurer transfers the certified sum from the General Fund to the Cash Reserve Fund (immediate transfer of the surplus portion; remainder by end of the following fiscal year), reduced as needed to keep the Cash Reserve Fund at or below 16% of budgeted General Fund expenditures (excluding reappropriations/encumbrances). Legislature may authorize exceeding 16%. Emergency clause: effective on enactment. Adds automatic year-end calculations and transfers involving the Tax Commissioner, Director of Administrative Services, and State Treasurer. Within 15 days after each fiscal year the Tax Commissioner must compute (i) the excess of actual over estimated General Fund net receipts and (ii) half of a growth-based formula using recent receipt increases. If (i) is positive, the Tax Commissioner certifies the larger of the two amounts to the Director of Administrative Services; upon that director’s certification the State Treasurer transfers the certified sum from the General Fund to the Cash Reserve Fund (the portion equal to (i) immediately; any remainder by the end of the next fiscal year). Transfers are reduced to prevent the Cash Reserve Fund exceeding 16% of budgeted General Fund expenditures unless the Legislature authorizes otherwise. DOCX | PDF

109-1-LB169_Intro General File Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB169_Intro_Copy.docx LB169 amends Nebraska tax law and reporting. The Department of Revenue must expand the annual Tax Expenditure Report to include estimated revenue loss from failure to impose sales and use tax on services purchased for nonbusiness use and to itemize specified service categories. The bill broadens the definition of "gross receipts" to expressly subject many services to sales/use tax (examples include vehicle and property maintenance and repair, personal and professional services, animal specialty and veterinary services except livestock, lodging-related receipts, and various personal care services). The Mechanical Amusement Device Tax Act is clarified to treat the occupation tax as additional to state taxes (including sales/use tax) and to prohibit local taxing of such devices except local option sales/use taxes. Operative October 1, 2025. No new appropriations or funding allocations are specified. Adds a long list of service categories (chartered flights; cleaning of clothing; dating services; hair care and removal; interior design; lobbying; local passenger chartered road transport (e.g., limousines); marketing/telemarketing; massage; nail care; personal instruction (dance, golf, tennis); ground sightseeing; skin care; swimming pool cleaning/maintenance; tattoo/body modification; telefloral delivery; travel agency; weight‑loss services) to the bill’s covered gross‑income provisions. It also expressly includes sales and use tax on gross receipts from operation of mechanical amusement devices (excluding local option sales/use taxes). No government agencies or departments are mentioned, and there are no funding, appropriation, or budget allocation changes in the added text. DOCX | PDF

109-1-LB174_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB174_Intro_Copy.docx LB174 amends Neb. Rev. The bill adds statutory definitions for health care services, medical debt, medical debt buyer, and medical creditor, and preserves existing exemptions (support orders, bankruptcy, tax). 109-1-LB177_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB177_Final_Copy.docx Department of Revenue This bill defines “Department” as the Department of Revenue and assigns several regulatory duties to it. 109-1-LB178_Intro General File Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB178_Intro_Copy.docx This bill directs the Nebraska Liquor Control Commission to establish and administer a mandatory server alcohol training program (effective Jan. 1, 2026) and to issue certificates to program completers. Retail licensees must employ only certified servers (or those within a 90‑day compliance window); the Commission may suspend, cancel, or revoke licenses for violations. The Commission may charge enrollment fees (≤ $30) and certification fees (≤ $20); fees are collected by the Commission, remitted to the State Treasurer, and credited to the Nebraska Liquor Control Commission Rule and Regulation Cash Fund. The fund’s purpose is expanded to include administering these provisions; monies may be invested by the state investment officer and transferred to the General Fund at the Legislature’s direction. Creates a mandatory server training program to be developed and administered by the Nebraska Liquor Control Commission (the commission) under section 6. The commission may charge an enrollment fee up to $30; all fees are collected by the commission and remitted to the State Treasurer for credit to the Nebraska Liquor Control Commission Rule and Regulation Cash Fund. Beginning January 1, 2026, retail liquor licensees may employ persons who sell, serve, mix alcohol, provide security, or verify age only if the person holds a commission‑approved server certification (or obtains it within 90 days). Licensees must keep certificates on the premises. The commission may suspend, cancel, or revoke licenses for violations. No other appropriations or budget increases are specified. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB179_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB179_Final_Copy.docx LB179 amends police and firefighters' retirement law for cities of the first class. It raises police officer employee contribution rates to the Police Officers Retirement System from 7% to 9% effective October 1, 2025, and continues the requirement that cities of the first class “pick up” those contributions (treated as employer contributions for federal tax purposes) with payment from the same municipal salary funding source. For the Cities of the First Class Firefighters Retirement Act, the retirement committee/city funding medium must permit optional benefit forms allowing single lump‑sum or partial distributions of a firefighter's retirement value (applicable for retirees on/after Jan 1, 1997); shortfalls to meet minimum pensions may be funded from the retirement system’s unallocated employer account. Operative date: Sections on optional distributions and repeal provisions take effect October 1, 2025. Adds two provisions affecting public safety retirement benefits: starting October 1, 2025, each police officer must contribute 9% of salary to the retirement system. 109-1-LB17_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB17_Intro_Copy.docx LB17 amends the Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act to prohibit most landlord fees, limit allowable fees, require written disclosure of total rent and itemized mandatory/optional fees, and require landlords to provide copies of any consumer reports plus the name, address, and phone number of each consumer reporting agency used. Enforcement: violations are treated as violations of Nebraska’s Consumer Protection Act (section 59-1602) and may be enforced by the Attorney General or by private civil action. Landlords who knowingly violate the section may incur civil penalties up to $300 per violation, plus court costs and attorney fees. The bill preserves rights under the state Credit Report Protection Act and the federal Fair Credit Reporting Act and references liability for improper dissemination of criminal history or FCRA violations. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. Adds limits on landlord fees and strong disclosure requirements. Landlords may only charge rent, security deposits (per §76-1416), returned-payment fees up to landlord cost, limited late fees, and application fees limited to the actual cost of obtaining a consumer report from a consumer reporting agency. Landlords must provide copies of any consumer/tenant screening reports and identify the consumer reporting agencies used, and must disclose total rent and itemized mandatory/optional fees before application. Optional services require written informed consent and opt-out. Violations are enforceable under the Consumer Protection Act by the aggrieved person or the Attorney General, with civil penalties up to $300 per violation plus costs. No funding or appropriation changes. DOCX | PDF

109-1-LB181_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB181_Intro_Copy.docx LB181 requires the Nebraska Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) to expand administration and federal-plan filings for the Young Adult Bridge to Independence Act to include young adults not lawfully present in the U.S. It amends verification rules so lawful-presence checks are not required for program participation. DHHS must: (1) submit a Title IV‑E state plan amendment (deadline previously set Oct 1, 2023) to secure IV‑E funding for newly eligible youth; (2) by Oct 1, 2025, apply to CMS to amend the Medicaid state plan to cover program participants (including non‑lawfully present under‑21s); and (3) adopt implementing rules by Oct 1, 2025. 109-1-LB206_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB206_Intro_Copy.docx LB206 (von Gillern) amends the Nebraska Criminal Code to impose enhanced penalties for specified offenses committed in a "disaster area" during an "emergency period." Disaster-area triggers include a Governor's emergency proclamation (see §81-829.40), a local emergency declaration (see §81-829.50), a presidential major disaster or emergency declaration under 42 U.S.C. §5121 et seq., or a mandatory evacuation order. Covered offenses (assaults, robbery, arson, burglary, theft, criminal mischief/trespass, and related inchoate and accomplice offenses) receive the next-higher penalty classification; a Class I misdemeanor upgrade becomes a Class IV felony. The indictment or information must allege the enhancement, and the prosecuting attorney must prove it beyond a reasonable doubt. No appropriations or budget changes are included. Adds definitions and penalty enhancements for crimes committed in disaster areas during an "emergency period." "Covered offense" lists numerous assault, robbery, arson, burglary, theft, criminal mischief/trespass statutes and related inchoate or accessory offenses. "Disaster area" is tied to: a Governor emergency proclamation (§81-829.40), local emergency declarations (§81-829.50), a Presidential major disaster/emergency (42 U.S.C. 5121 et seq.), or mandatory evacuation orders by appropriate local, state, or federal officials. An emergency period ends with the proclamation/declaration/order or 30 days after issuance if no end date is provided. Penalties are bumped to the next higher classification (Class I misdemeanor → Class IV felony); enhancements must be alleged in the indictment/information and proven beyond a reasonable doubt by the prosecuting attorney. No funding, appropriation, or budget changes are included. DOCX | PDF

109-1-LB211_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB211_Intro_Copy.docx LB211 amends calculation of a political subdivision’s property tax request authority under the Property Tax Growth Limitation Act. The preliminary authority is set equal to the prior fiscal year property taxes levied by the county board of equalization less exceptions under §13-3404. Political subdivisions may increase that authority by two components (growth and inflation) based on whether public safety (per §13-320) comprises ≥20% of their property-tax-funded budget. If ≥20%, the inflation component is the greater of zero or the inflation percentage; if <20%, the inflation component is the greater of two percent or the inflation percentage. The bill repeals the original §13-3403 and takes effect immediately. Adds a formula letting a political subdivision increase its property tax request authority based on prior-year levies (minus exceptions under A.R.S. §13-3404(1)–(2)), its growth percentage, and inflation. If public safety services (per §13-320) are ≥20% of the subdivision’s property-tax-funded budget, the inflation component is the greater of zero or actual inflation (no minimum). If public safety services are <20%, the inflation component is the greater of 2% or actual inflation (a 2% floor). No new agency appropriations are specified; the change alters how local governments’ (political subdivisions’) property-tax increases are calculated. DOCX | PDF

For retail dealers, tax is triggered when ENDS are brought into the state, manufactured in-state for sale, or sold to consumers. Collections are to be used and distributed pursuant to §77-4025. 109-1-LB216_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB216_Intro_Copy.docx LB216 centralizes district-court clerical functions under the judicial branch and shifts related funding to the State.\n\nKey agency actions and fiscal changes:\n- Beginning January 7, 2027, elected clerks of the district court and their employees transfer to state employment under the Nebraska Supreme Court; salaries, benefits, and expenses to be paid by the State with funds appropriated to the Supreme Court. Transferred staff become subject to Supreme Court personnel rules.\n- Counties must provide accrual data; counties reimburse the State (and employees) per statutory formulas for transferred sick leave (25% of value) and vacation leave (100% for transferred hours); counties remain owners of furniture/equipment while books/files transfer to the State Court Administrator.\n- Retirement transfers handled under existing systems (Retirement System for Nebraska Counties or State Employees Retirement System) with cost‑sharing intent to prevent benefit loss.\n- The State will fund specified district/separate juvenile court IT and communications operational costs via the Supreme Court.\n- Federal reimbursements for child/spousal/medical support costs received on behalf of clerks are to be remitted to the State Treasurer for credit to Agency 5 – Supreme Court.\n- Department of Health and Human Services will receive required court statistical reports; the State Court Administrator negotiates reimbursement agreements on behalf of clerks.\n- Oaths filed with the Secretary of State; clerks are prohibited from serving on mental-health boards. Key additions:\n\n- Effective Jan 7, 2027, elected clerks of the district court and their employees transfer to state employment under the Nebraska Supreme Court; State Court Administrator handles records transfer and appointment/management rules apply for vacancies. \n- The State of Nebraska, using funds appropriated to the Supreme Court, will pay all salaries, benefits, and expenses of transferred clerks/employees. Transferred staff keep employment unless removed for cause under Supreme Court personnel rules. \n- Counties retain furniture/equipment but must transfer books/files to the State Court Administrator. \n- Leave and retirement: accrued sick leave (up to 1,440 hours) transfers; county reimburses state 25% of its value (excess sick reimbursed 25% to employee). Vacation transfer cap 280 hours; county reimburses state 100% of transferred vacation value (excess reimbursed 100% to employee). Retirement-cost sharing and SERS/County Retirement System provisions govern benefit continuity. \n- State will pay certain court IT and communications operational costs from Supreme Court appropriations. \n- Federal reimbursements for direct costs are to the State Treasurer for credit to Agency 5 – Supreme Court. All DHHS child welfare staff who provide or directly interact with children/families, and other personnel designated by the Division of Children and Family Services, must receive annual training and training prior to any independent contact; training will be delivered within existing department programs. DHHS must also: (1) include this suicide prevention training in initial licensure and license renewal processes referenced in sections 71‑1901 to 71‑1906.01, and (2) set standardized pre‑contact training requirements for employees of child‑placing agencies while allowing agencies to use or adapt approved curricula that meet the baseline. 109-1-LB222_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB222_Intro_Copy.docx LB222 amends Nebraska Rules of the Road and related statutes to limit routine traffic-stop and search powers of peace officers while preserving full enforcement authority for the Superintendent of Law Enforcement and Public Safety and Nebraska State Patrol officers (with carrier enforcement officers excepted). Key agency impacts:\n- Superintendent of Law Enforcement and Public Safety and Nebraska State Patrol: retain powers under section 81-2005; sections 3–4’s restrictions do not apply to them.\n- Peace officers: prohibited from stopping/detaining drivers for nonmoving violations, suspended-license offenses under specified sections, and certain misdemeanor warrants; equipment-failure stops allowed only for objectively immediate, serious safety threats and require pre-stop logging/dispatch notice and on-contact explanations.\n- Searches: officers must obtain a warrant or written consent from the vehicle’s operator using a prescribed form (English/Spanish, right to counsel, voluntary/revocable); evidence from violations of this section is inadmissible.\nNo funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. The bill takes effect immediately under an emergency clause. Adds limits on law-enforcement stops, detentions, and vehicle searches. Key points: peace officers may not stop for most nonmoving or certain misdemeanor/warrant violations and may stop for equipment failures only if the defect relates to the vehicle and poses an objectively reasonable, immediate serious safety threat. Searches otherwise require a warrant or written consent from the vehicle operator, using a prescribed form (explaining voluntariness, right to counsel, ability to revoke consent) available in English and Spanish and explained via interpreter if needed. Evidence obtained in violation is inadmissible. No specific state agencies, departments, or funding/appropriation changes are named. DOCX | PDF

109-1-LB224_Intro General File Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB224_Intro_Copy.docx LB224 requires the State of Nebraska to provide paid maternity leave for state employees. Key provisions: full‑time state employees who give birth and assume a parental role are entitled to 12 weeks paid leave (part‑time leave prorated). Leave may not begin before birth, must be used within six months, is generally non‑intermittent (unless by mutual written agreement or a health‑care provider certifies medical necessity), and runs concurrently with federal Family and Medical Leave Act protections. Leave is not charged to sick, vacation, compensatory, or other leave. Employees are protected from defined retaliatory actions and are guaranteed return to their prior or an equivalent position. No appropriations, funding increases, or budget allocations are specified in the bill. Creates a state-paid maternity leave program for state employees: full‑time state employees receive 12 weeks paid leave (part‑time prorated) to bond with a newborn. Leave may not start before birth, must be used within six months, is limited to 12 weeks per 12‑month period, generally cannot be charged against other leave, runs concurrently with federal FMLA, and may be intermittent only by written agreement or medical certification. Defines “state employee,” “maternity leave eligible employee,” and “retaliatory action,” and guarantees return to the same or equivalent position. Mentions health care provider and FMLA (29 U.S.C. 2601 et seq.). No agencies, appropriations, or new funding/budget allocations are specified. DOCX | PDF

The bill preserves similar sealing procedures for sex‑trafficking victims, pardoned persons, and certain pre‑2017 dismissals. It creates a private cause of action against state agencies, political subdivisions, and their officers/employees for violations of the Security, Privacy, and Dissemination of Criminal History Information Act, expressly waives sovereign immunity for such suits, excludes these suits from the State/Political Subdivisions Tort Claims Acts, sets remedies (including damages and equitable relief), and provides a limitations period. No funding or appropriation changes are included. Adds two main provisions. First, creates a process to set aside convictions or juvenile adjudications for “concealed weapon” offenses (defined) — motions filed in the convicting juvenile/county/district court; courts weigh post‑sentence behavior and public welfare; a rebuttable presumption favors relief if the underlying conduct would not now violate current law; an order setting aside must have the same effect as existing set‑aside orders and authorizes a follow‑on motion to seal the criminal history (court must grant sealing and issue required orders).\n\nSecond, establishes private liability for violations of rules under the Security, Privacy, and Dissemination of Criminal History Information Act: the state, any state agency or political subdivision, and their officers/employees may be joined as defendants (sovereign immunity waived); remedies include actual damages, equitable relief, and writs; actions are exempt from the State Tort Claims Act and Political Subdivisions Tort Claims Act; filing deadlines: later of four years after accrual or by Jan 1, 2029 in specified cases. 109-1-LB247_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB247_Final_Copy.docx LB247 amends provisions administered by the Department of Environment and Energy concerning solid‑waste disposal fees and the Petroleum Release Remedial Action Cash Fund. Landfill/processing operators must pay a disposal fee of $2.34 per applicable unit quarterly to the department. Receipts are split 65% to the Integrated Solid Waste Management Cash Fund (for the department’s response to spills/environmental emergencies; regulation, investigation, remediation and monitoring; CERCLA nonfederal cost‑share, O&M and related activities) and 35% to the Waste Reduction and Recycling Incentive Fund (grants to local governments and reimbursements for dump‑site remediation, with political‑subdivision reimbursements capped at 5% of prior‑year disposal fee revenue). The Petroleum Release Remedial Action Cash Fund (administered by the department) receives fee revenue, settlements, gifts and appropriations and may be used for remedial actions, department response costs, State Fire Marshal fee collection expenses, State Claims Board‑approved claims, and investment earnings are credited to the fund. 109-1-LB249_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB249_Intro_Copy.docx LB249 (109th Leg., 1st Sess.) directs the Department (Nebraska Department of Education) to implement a new military impact funding stream beginning FY2025‑26 for districts that received federal impact aid under ESEA §7003 and educate federally connected active‑duty children. The Department must calculate payments per a defined formula (difference between per‑pupil local general fund tax levy and per‑pupil federal impact aid, multiplied by federally connected pupils; floor at zero). The bill resets certification timelines: state aid, district budget authority, and allowable reserve percentages are to be certified by the Department on or before June 15, 2025 and March 1 thereafter; any such certifications made earlier for FY2025‑26 are nullified. The Appropriations Committee must include funding necessary to cover certified state aid in its budget recommendations. The act takes effect immediately. Effective for school fiscal year 2025‑26 onward, the state "department" (state education department context) must determine and pay military impact funding to eligible school districts. Eligibility requires the district received a federal impact aid basic support payment under §7003 of the federal Elementary and Secondary Education Act in the prior year and educates federally connected children whose parents are on active duty. The statute defines calculation: per‑pupil federal impact aid = prior year federal payment ÷ number of active‑duty federally connected students (fall count); per‑pupil general fund tax levy = prior year local property tax levy ÷ fall membership excluding those federally connected students. Military impact funding = (per‑pupil tax levy − per‑pupil federal aid) × number of active‑duty federally connected students, floored at zero. No specific appropriation or new budget totals are provided. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB24_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB24_Intro_Copy.docx LB24 amends probation fee and revocation statutes. District and county courts must assess a $30 one-time administrative enrollment fee and monthly programming fees ($25 for standard probation; $35 for intensive supervision and participants in non‑probation programs that use probation personnel under interlocal agreements funded in part by §29‑2262.07). Clerks of court remit collected fees to the State Treasurer for credit to the Probation Program Cash Fund. Courts may remove non‑probation program participants for fee default; waivers are available for persons previously found indigent or who show undue hardship. Adult probationers received under the Interstate Compact are assessed while actively supervised by Nebraska probation authorities. For felony probationers, revocation for substance‑abuse or noncriminal violations is permitted only after the probationer has served 90 days of cumulative custodial sanctions in the current term. Adds authority for courts to waive the fees referenced in §29-2262(2)(m) and (o) if the offender was previously found indigent in the case or, after a hearing, if payment would be an undue hardship. The waiver applies only while the probationer or a participant in a non-probation-based program is unable to pay the monthly probation programming fee. Also allows the probation term to be extended, at the joint request of the probationer and the prosecutor, while a motion or information to revoke probation is pending or until the statutory maximum probation period expires; the court must accept the extension if the probationer has counsel or knowingly and voluntarily requests it in open court. Agencies mentioned: courts and prosecutors. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB250_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB250_Final_Copy.docx LB250 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §8-126 to revise residency and qualification rules for bank directors. It requires reasonable efforts that a majority of a bank’s board have primary residences (a) in Nebraska, (b) within 25 miles of the bank’s main office, (c) in the county of the main office, or (d) in counties where the bank has branches. Directors must be persons of good moral character, integrity and business experience and may not serve until approved by the department (the Department of Banking and Finance). The Director of Banking and Finance is authorized, after investigation and hearing, to revoke a director’s approval for unsafe or unauthorized conduct, and to adopt rules, regulations, and forms to implement the section. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. The added language requires that "reasonable efforts shall be made" regarding a party/act described as "a to primary" and lists options (a)–(d). No specific government agencies or departments are named, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations included in this insertion. The provision imposes a general duty to undertake efforts but does not identify implementing entities or financial impacts. DOCX | PDF

The Director may adopt rules to implement insider/executive lending limits (sec. 8‑143.01) consistent with 12 U.S.C. 84/Reg O (as of 1/1/2025). The Department of Insurance is given sole authority (and rulemaking power) over issuance/sale of funding agreements by admitted life insurers. 109-1-LB252_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB252_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Health and Human Services The bill amends the Medical Assistance Act (section 68-901) to add a new requirement for the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS). DHHS must ensure its Medicaid formulary and preferred drug list do not disadvantage or discourage FDA‑approved non‑opioid pain drugs relative to opioids — including prohibiting designation of a non‑opioid as nonpreferred when an opioid is preferred and barring more restrictive utilization controls (e.g., prior authorization, step therapy) for non‑opioids than the least restrictive controls for opioids. The requirement applies immediately upon FDA approval and to drugs provided under DHHS contracts with managed care organizations. The bill contains no funding, appropriation, or budget allocation changes. Requires the Department of Health and Human Services, when setting and maintaining the Medicaid formulary and preferred drug list, to ensure any FDA‑approved non‑opioid pain treatment is not disadvantaged versus opioids. Impermissible actions include designating a non‑opioid as nonpreferred while an opioid is preferred and imposing more restrictive utilization controls (e.g., prior authorization, step therapy) on a non‑opioid than the least restrictive controls applied to an opioid. The rule takes effect for a non‑opioid immediately upon FDA approval and covers drugs provided under DHHS contracts with managed care organizations. It does not prevent preferring one opioid over another or one non‑opioid over another. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB253_Intro General File Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB253_Intro_Copy.docx LB253 requires health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, health maintenance organizations, and Nebraska’s medical assistance program (administered by the Department of Health and Human Services) to cover biomarker testing for diagnosis, treatment, management, or monitoring when supported by medical/scientific evidence, including FDA approvals/labels, FDA-indicated drug tests and warnings, CMS national or Medicare administrative contractor local coverage determinations, or nationally recognized clinical guidelines. The medical assistance program must implement coverage by January 1, 2026; its contractors must provide testing at the same scope, duration, and frequency. Prior authorization decisions must be issued within 72 hours (nonurgent) or 24 hours (urgent). Insurers and DHHS must post an accessible exception/appeals process on their websites. The bill contains no appropriations, funding changes, or budget allocations. Adds mandatory coverage standards for biomarker testing, including for the state medical assistance program (required no later than Jan 1, 2026). Tests must be covered when supported by medical/scientific evidence such as: FDA-approved/cleared labeled indications, FDA‑indicated tests for drugs, FDA drug label warnings/precautions, CMS national coverage determinations or local Medicare administrative contractor determinations, and nationally recognized clinical practice guidelines. Entities contracting with the medical assistance program must provide testing at the same scope/duration/frequency as the program. Prior authorization decisions/notifications must occur within 72 hours (nonurgent) or 24 hours (urgent) for insurers and the medical assistance program (or their third‑party agents). Exception request processes must be posted on insurer websites and the Department of Health and Human Services website. No funding or appropriation changes are included. DOCX | PDF

109-1-LB255_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB255_Intro_Copy.docx LB255 amends statutes to allow and prioritize use of the newly created Opioid Treatment Infrastructure Cash Fund (funded by transfers from the Nebraska Opioid Recovery Trust Fund) for Supreme Court problem-solving courts to order medication-assisted treatment (MAT). 109-1-LB256_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB256_Intro_Copy.docx LB256 adopts the Midwest Interstate Passenger Rail Compact, creating a multistate commission to coordinate Midwestern intercity and high‑speed passenger rail planning and advocacy. The commission is authorized to work with federal agencies, members of Congress, state and local officials, economic development bodies, and rail industry stakeholders; establish offices and hire staff; accept grants, gifts, and appropriations from the federal government, party states, agencies, or municipalities; and must submit budgets to the officer designated under each member state’s law. Financing of commission operations is by appropriation of compacting states (equal apportionment, when legislatures authorize). The commission may not issue debt. Nebraska may not participate in or appropriate funds for any compact rail project (including planning) unless a legislative bill specifically authorizes it. The bill creates the Midwest Interstate Passenger Rail Compact Cash Fund, with investment by the state investment officer under applicable Nebraska investment statutes. Adds Nebraska-specific limits and a dedicated fund. Nebraska may not participate in or appropriate money for any Midwest Interstate Passenger Rail Compact project — including planning — unless a specific legislative bill authorizes that project. Creates the "Midwest Interstate Passenger Rail Compact Cash Fund" to hold gifts, grants, bequests (federal, state, public, private) and transfers from the Nebraska Legislature; monies must be used for Compact passenger rail initiatives. Funds available for investment must be invested by the state investment officer under the Nebraska Capital Expansion Act and the Nebraska State Funds Investment Act. The commission may also receive federal, state, or local department/agency/municipal appropriations; member-state operating funding requires legislative authorization and equal apportionment. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB257_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB257_Final_Copy.docx LB257 makes credentialing and licensing changes and assigns duties to several state agencies and boards.\n\n- Department (with board recommendation): May issue licenses/certificates to marriage and family therapists based on out-of-state licensure (requires Nebraska jurisprudence exam); expands and clarifies occupational therapy definitions, scope (new modality definitions), supervision rules, certification for dry needling, and training/examination authority for modalities administered by therapists and assistants.\n\n- Department of Health and Human Services (referred to as department in Child Care Licensing Act): Requires written proof of liability insurance ($100,000 per occurrence) before licensing and continuous maintenance; inspectors must verify insurance at unannounced inspections and may suspend licenses if coverage lapses (3 business-day cure). Department may seek federal funds to subsidize fingerprinting/national criminal history checks; otherwise applicants/staff bear costs. Background checks (FBI via Nebraska State Patrol, NSOPR, state registries) are required and portable; employers with disqualified staff are ineligible for licensing or subsidy.\n\n- Nebraska State Patrol: Conducts fingerprint transmission to FBI.\n\n- State Fire Marshal: May inspect programs for fire safety at the department's request. Adds procedures for licensing and certification administered by "the department, with the recommendation of the board": recognition of out‑of‑state marriage and family therapist licensure (requiring a valid unrestricted license, application/fees, and passing the Nebraska jurisprudence exam); issuance of certificates for occupational therapists to use dry needling after board‑approved training; and board approval of examinations and training for physical‑agent and instrument‑assisted modalities. Defines supervision responsibilities for occupational therapists, assistants, and aides, and restricts delegation of evaluations, treatment planning, and certain modalities. Strengthens enforcement: inspectors must verify liability insurance, the department must notify licensees of lapses, and may suspend licenses if proof is not provided within three business days (see §71‑1911.03). No funding or appropriation changes. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB258_Final Final Reading Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB258_Final_Copy.docx Department of Labor LB258 assigns two administrative duties to the Nebraska Department of Labor and its Commissioner. Beginning Oct. 15, 2026, and each Oct. 15 thereafter, the Department must calculate and publish the minimum wage rate that will take effect the following Jan. 1. Separately, the Commissioner of Labor must approve on‑the‑job training programs if an employer seeks to extend a new hire’s training‑wage period by an additional 90 days (no more than one‑fourth of total employer hours may be at the training rate). The bill does not include any changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department of Labor. Adds statutory youth and training wage schedules. Employers may pay 14‑ and 15‑year‑old non‑emancipated employees a youth minimum wage of $13.50/hr; that youth wage will increase 1.5% (rounded to nearest cent) beginning Jan 1, 2030 and every five years thereafter. The training wage is set at $13.50/hr through Dec 31, 2026, then will rise 1.5% (rounded to nearest cent) annually starting Jan 1, 2027. The amendment does not specify any Department of Labor funding, appropriations, or budget allocations or create new financial appropriations; it merely sets wage rates and adjustment schedules (no explicit DOL administrative or budgetary changes are included). 109-1-LB259_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB259_Intro_Copy.docx LB259 (Faithful Delegate to Federal Article V Convention Act) prescribes how Nebraska’s Legislature will select, instruct, oversee, and, if necessary, remove members of a state delegation to a U.S. Article V convention. Key government bodies named: the Committee on Committees (nominates one delegate and one alternate per legislative caucus), the full Legislature (elects delegates/alternates, adopts/amends instructions, determines unauthorized votes), the Executive Board of the Legislative Council together with the Lieutenant Governor (serve as the advisory committee when the Legislature is not in session), the Speaker of the Legislature (notifies convention officers of disqualifications), and the Secretary of State (receives delegates’ oaths). Delegates receive no pay but may be reimbursed under statutes sections 81-1174 to 81-1177. Gifts from registered lobbyists are prohibited (violations Class III misdemeanor). No new appropriations or budget allocations are included. Adds a statutory framework for selecting, instructing, and policing state Article V convention delegates. Agencies/departments mentioned and roles:\n- Legislature: adopts delegate instructions, elects delegates/alternates, determines unauthorized votes, fills vacancies.\n- Committee on Committees of the Legislature: nominates one delegate and alternate per legislative caucus.\n- Executive Board of the Legislative Council and Lieutenant Governor: form the advisory committee (chair = executive board chair; Lt. Governor breaks ties) to act when the Legislature is not in session.\n- Speaker of the Legislature: must notify convention officers of disqualifications.\n- Secretary of State: receives delegates' oaths.\n- References to Nebraska Political Accountability and Disclosure Act, Secretary of the U.S. Senate and Clerk of the U.S. House (lobbyist registries), and reimbursement rules in sections 81-1174 to 81-1177.\n\nFunding/appropriations: delegates/alternates receive no compensation but may be reimbursed for expenses under existing statutes; no new appropriations specified. DOCX | PDF

109-1-LB266_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB266_Final_Copy.docx LB266 forbids local governments—defined as any city, village, county, or any agency or subdivision thereof—from enacting or enforcing ordinances that have the effect of imposing rent controls on private property. Exceptions allow ordinances that increase affordable housing supply via land‑use or inclusionary housing requirements and voluntary, contract‑based programs where property owners agree to rent restrictions. The prohibition overrides home‑rule charters, and any conflicting local ordinance is declared null and void. No state agencies, departments, or budgetary changes, appropriations, or funding shifts are specified in the bill. Adds a statewide prohibition on local governments (defined to include cities, villages, counties and their agencies or subdivisions) from enacting or enforcing ordinances that impose rent control on private property. "Ordinance" is defined broadly to include ordinances, resolutions, rules, or regulations. Exceptions permit local measures that (1) increase the supply of affordable housing through land‑use or inclusionary housing requirements, or (2) create voluntary, contract‑based programs in which private owners agree to limit rents. The prohibition overrides home rule charters, and any conflicting local ordinance is declared null and void. No state agencies, departments, or funding/appropriations changes are referenced. 109-1-LB267_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB267_Intro_Copy.docx LB267 amends the Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act to allow tenants who have a protective/ restraining order or certified domestic-violence documentation to remove a cotenant or occupant who perpetrated the violence from the rental agreement. It directs landlords to serve eviction notices and, if necessary, file suit in court for possession solely against the perpetrator; courts may award the landlord court costs and reasonable attorney’s fees. Landlords must install new locks (or rekey/reset codes) and notify the tenant how to obtain access; law enforcement may be required to escort a perpetrator reclaiming property. No state agency or department is specifically created or referenced beyond courts and law enforcement, and the bill contains no appropriations or funding changes. Adds tenant protections when domestic violence occurs: a tenant with a protective order or certified domestic-violence documentation can (1) have a cotenant/perpetrator removed from the rental agreement (landlord must pursue possession actions in court against the perpetrator only; landlord may recover court costs and reasonable attorney’s fees if judgment is entered) and (2) require a landlord to change or rekey locks within 24 hours when the perpetrator is not a cotenant. Landlords may require reimbursement for actual lock-change costs; tenants may change locks if landlord fails. The bill references courts (judicial proceedings) and law enforcement officers (required to escort a perpetrator reclaiming property). No agencies, departments, or budget/appropriation changes are specified. DOCX | PDF

109-1-LB272_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB272_Intro_Copy.docx LB272 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §77-3506 to expand homestead tax exemptions and to specify certification requirements from the United States Department of Veterans Affairs (VA). The bill requires VA certification of veteran/spouse status: certain 100% categories require application and VA certification every five years, while other eligible categories require annual application but VA certification only every five years. 109-1-LB273_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB273_Intro_Copy.docx LB273 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §30-3417 governing powers of an attorney-in-fact under a health care power of attorney. It narrows attorney-in-fact authority (e.g., may not consent to acts the principal could not lawfully consent to; may not make decisions that will cause the death of an unborn child likely to reach live birth unless the treating physician finds the principal’s life at risk; and may not withhold/withdraw life‑sustaining treatment or artificially administered nutrition and hydration except as provided in §30‑3418). The bill affirms the county court’s role: a principal’s objection controls unless a county court determines incapacity. It also requires health care providers to have a signed original or copy before accepting decisions. No agencies, departments, or budgetary appropriations are created or amended. Adds a clause describing an exception when an act "will result in the death of the principal's unborn child and the unborn child is likely to [do so]" unless the principal's treating physician determines the principal's life is at risk. 109-1-LB274_Intro Indefinitely postponed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB274_Intro_Copy.docx LB274 amends the Child Care Licensing Act to tighten insurance verification, inspection, and background-check procedures. The Department (agency administering licensing) must obtain written proof of liability insurance of at least $200,000 per occurrence before issuing a license and verify current coverage at each unannounced inspection; failure to provide proof within three business days triggers license suspension until coverage is verified. The Department may request State Fire Marshal inspections and may delegate sanitation and facility investigations to local environmental health personnel or city/village/county authorities. The Nebraska State Patrol will process fingerprints and transmit them to the FBI; the Department will provide criminal-history documentation, require periodic background checks, and seek federal funds to offset fingerprinting costs. If federal funds are insufficient, applicants/staff or licensees bear the cost; the Department may cover costs if funding becomes available. No direct appropriations or budget allocations are specified. Adds requirement that licensees must continuously maintain required liability insurance and that inspectors must request and verify current proof at each unannounced inspection and each investigation. If proof is missing or coverage lapsed, the department will demand proof within three business days and will suspend the license if proof is not provided; licensure is restored when the department verifies the insurance per section 71‑1911.03. No agencies beyond "the department"/inspectors are newly created or referenced, and no funding or appropriation changes are included. DOCX | PDF

109-1-LB275_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB275_Final_Copy.docx Department of Health and Human Services The bill amends duties of the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) regarding children under its charge. DHHS must take custody/control of children’s assets, screen each child for Social Security eligibility within 60 days, submit applications and appeal denials, and, when serving as representative payee, manage, conserve, and hold benefit payments separate from department funds (including use of trusts and accounts to avoid federal asset/resource limits). It must conserve minimum percentages of benefits by age, provide accounting and written notice at review hearings, consult with beneficiaries 14+ at least semiannually, assist with benefit applications before discharge, and deliver an exit notice. By October 1, 2026, DHHS must create a beneficiary request form and adopt implementing rules. DHHS shall maximize federal Title IV‑E funding before using General Funds for implementation costs. The Department of Health and Human Services must screen each child in its care for Social Security benefit eligibility within 60 days and apply (and appeal if needed). If DHHS is representative payee, it must manage payments per federal law: hold funds separate (trust account), conserve age-based minimum percentages (14+ 20%; 16+ 30%; 17+ 40%; 18+ 50%), avoid exceeding federal asset limits by using allowable accounts (e.g., PASS, ABLE, IDA, special‑needs trust), and send unspent funds to the child on exit. Children (14+) get semiannual consultation and may seek juvenile‑court orders on use. DHHS must provide notices, accounting on request, a public access form by Oct 1, 2026, and assist with benefit continuity before discharge. For implementation costs, DHHS must maximize federal Title IV‑E funding before using General Funds. No specific appropriations are included. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB276_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB276_Intro_Copy.docx LB276 creates the Municipal Police Oversight Act and amends law enforcement record and reporting duties. Key governmental duties and agencies:\n\n- Cities of metropolitan or primary class must create seven‑member citizen police oversight boards by Jan 1, 2028; boards receive subpoenas, inspect police records, investigate complaints and officer‑involved shootings, consult standards from the Nebraska Commission on Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice and the Nebraska Police Standards Advisory Council, and publish findings (Open Meetings Act applies). Police departments must respond to board recommendations.\n\n- City attorneys, county attorneys, and the Attorney General must maintain and post public Brady/Giglio lists (updated monthly) beginning Sept 1, 2025; the Nebraska Commission on Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice will adopt implementing rules by Sept 1, 2025.\n\n- Prohibits issuance of no‑knock warrants.\n\n- Agencies must submit officer hires/separations to the training center director within seven days; serious‑conduct records retained permanently and terminations/resignations for serious conduct reported to the Commission within 30 days. No appropriations or funding changes. Emergency clause—effective on enactment. Adds a Municipal Police Oversight Act requiring every metropolitan or primary-class city that employs full‑time police officers to create a seven‑member citizen oversight board by Jan 1, 2028. Boards (appointed by city council; no current/former city or county law‑enforcement employees) may: investigate complaints, shootings, discrimination/harassment, and misconduct; inspect police and personnel records; issue subpoenas; refer evidence to county attorneys; report to the police department, mayor, council, and federal/state registries; and consult standards from the Nebraska Commission on Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice and the Nebraska Police Standards Advisory Council. Boards’ reports and police responses are public records; meetings must comply with the Open Meetings Act. Beginning Sept 1, 2025, city attorneys, county attorneys, and the Attorney General must maintain and post Brady/Giglio lists (updated monthly); the Nebraska Commission must adopt implementing rules. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB277_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB277_Intro_Copy.docx Bill amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §29-1401 to tighten grand-jury procedures for deaths during apprehension or custody. District courts must call a grand jury when the county coroner or coroner’s physician certifies such a death. The court must, as soon as practicable, appoint a special prosecutor (minimum five years’ felony/criminal litigation experience) who will select a three-officer homicide-investigation team drawn from outside the jurisdiction to examine evidence and report to the special prosecutor. Local law enforcement must secure the scene, preserve evidence, and transfer assembled materials to the special prosecutor. A grand jury must be impaneled within 30 days unless extended. Officers or detention personnel involved may not return to duty until grand-jury proceedings conclude. A special prosecutor is not required if a licensed physician certifies natural causes and the county attorney presents that finding. No appropriations or funding changes. Adds that the court must appoint a special prosecutor with at least five years' experience in criminal litigation, including felony cases. It also suggests limited exceptions for appointing a special prosecutor in other jurisdictions (text is partially fragmented). Requires any law‑enforcement officer or detention personnel involved in a death to remain off duty until the grand jury completes its investigation. No government funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are mentioned. DOCX | PDF

109-1-LB27_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB27_Intro_Copy.docx This bill amends the Rural Health Systems and Professional Incentive Act and the Medicaid Managed Care Excess Profit Fund. It (1) explicitly allows the Excess Profit Fund to be used for loan repayments under the Rural Health Act and confirms fund investment by the state investment officer with investment earnings credited to the General Fund beginning October 1, 2024; (2) restates the Act’s purposes, including creating the Nebraska Rural Health Advisory Commission; (3) creates a new dentist loan-repayment pathway administered by the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) for early-career dentists who commit to five years’ practice in Nebraska with specified Medicaid patient thresholds, authorizing DHHS payments up to $60,000/year (maximum $300,000) for up to five years; (4) requires repayments under that dentist option to be made only from specifically appropriated funds and expresses legislative intent to appropriate $1.5 million from the Medicaid Managed Care Excess Profit Fund to DHHS for FY2025–26. Creates a loan repayment program administered by the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS), exempting agreements from the State Procurement Act, to recruit dentists who treat Medicaid patients. Eligible dentists must have <5 years' practice and no prior Rural Health Systems and Professional Incentive Act assistance. Agreements (in lieu of section 71-5668 contracts) require five years' Nebraska practice and a commission‑determined Medicaid patient threshold. DHHS may pay qualified educational debt up to $60,000/year per recipient (up to $300,000 total); recipients must verify funds were used for debt. Breach requires full repayment with 8% simple interest; obligations cancel on death or total permanent disability. DHHS may only use specifically appropriated funds; Legislature intends to appropriate $1.5 million from the Medicaid Managed Care Excess Profit Fund for FY2025‑26. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB280_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB280_Intro_Copy.docx LB280 amends Nebraska racetrack gaming law to (1) authorize the State Racing and Gaming Commission to administer and enforce a new annual audit requirement (section 7) and to use the Racing and Gaming Commission’s Racetrack Gaming Fund to pay for any audit, examination, or review required or authorized under that section; and (2) require every authorized gaming operator to obtain, at its expense, an annual independent CPA audit (including internal control report) of Nebraska operations and submit it electronically to the Auditor of Public Accounts and the gaming commission within six months (subject to extension). The Auditor of Public Accounts must review audit reports for mathematical or accounting deficiencies—especially those affecting gross gaming revenue or gaming tax—and report results to the Governor, the Legislature, and the gaming commission, and may examine operators’ books, records, funds, and accounts as prescribed. Investment earnings on the fund are credited to the General Fund. No specific dollar appropriations are included. Added provisions require each authorized gaming operator to obtain, at its own expense, an annual independent CPA audit (including an internal control report) of all Nebraska financial transactions for the preceding fiscal year. The audit must be submitted electronically within six months after year-end to the Auditor of Public Accounts and the gaming commission (Auditor may grant a written extension). The Auditor of Public Accounts will review the audit for calculation errors, improper accounting, or other deficiencies—particularly those affecting gross gaming revenue or the annual gaming tax—and will report the review results electronically to the Governor, the Legislature, and the gaming commission. No new funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified. DOCX | PDF

109-1-LB285_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB285_Intro_Copy.docx LB285 amends Nebraska law to prohibit the marketing, sale, and tax certification of flavored electronic nicotine delivery systems (ENDS). It bars licensees under the retail tobacco licensing scheme (secs. 28-1420 to 28-1429) from selling flavored vapor products and prohibits manufacturers from causing such products to be sold at retail in the state. The Tax Commissioner and the cigarette tax division are empowered to refuse issuance of Tobacco Products Tax Act certifications for flavored ENDS and to revoke or suspend relevant licenses or certifications for violations; contraband provisions and seizure/forfeiture authority for unlawful cigarette imports are retained. The bill does not include any funding, appropriation, or budget allocation changes. Adds a definition of "flavored vapor product" for electronic nicotine delivery systems (any product with a taste/smell other than tobacco or menthol — e.g., mint, fruit, candy, dessert, alcohol, herbs/spices — marketed or claimed as such). Key agency/actor provisions:\n- Persons holding licenses under sections 28-1420 to 28-1429 are prohibited from marketing, advertising, selling, or causing the sale of flavored vapor products.\n- The Tax Commissioner is barred from issuing certifications under section 77-4011.01 for any electronic nicotine delivery system that is a flavored vapor product.\n- Manufacturers are prohibited from causing flavored electronic nicotine delivery systems to be sold at retail in the state.\n\nNo changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. 109-1-LB287_Intro Governor Veto Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB287_Intro_Copy.docx LB287 amends the Nebraska Housing Agency Act (section 71-1572) to impose specific bed-bug duties on housing agencies for cities of the metropolitan class. Agencies must visually inspect units before renting, not lease units known or reasonably suspected to be infested, disclose adjacent-unit treatments, and respond to complaints with acknowledgement (within 5 days), inspection by or procurement of a licensed pest control professional (within 5 days), remediation if infestation is confirmed (within 14 days), adjacent-unit inspections, tenant notice before entry, notice of determinations (within 5 days), and two-year retention of complaint/control records. The bill defines pest control professional as a commercial applicator under the Pesticide Act and makes the housing agency financially responsible for investigation and remediation costs. No specific appropriations or new budget allocations are included. Original section repealed. Adds requirements for the "housing agency for a city of the metropolitan class." Key points:\n- Defines "bed bug" and "pest control professional" (must be a commercial applicator licensed under the Pesticide Act).\n- Imposes pre-rental duties: visual inspection for bed bugs, prohibition on showing/renting units known or reasonably suspected to be infested, and disclosure to prospective tenants if adjacent units are infested or being treated.\n- Sets response timelines after a complaint: acknowledge within 5 days; inspect or hire a pest control professional within 5 days; inspect adjacent units within 5 days; provide remediation within 14 days after infestation is confirmed; notify affected tenants of findings within 5 days; give advance notice before entering units; keep written records (including chemicals used) for two years.\n- Fiscal change: the housing agency is made responsible for all costs of investigating and remediating bed bug infestations. 109-1-LB293_Final Passed Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB293_Final_Copy.docx LB293 amends the Professional Employer Organization Registration Act. It requires any self‑funded health benefit plan offered by a PEO to use a third‑party administrator licensed in Nebraska, hold plan assets in an ERISA section 403 trust, maintain actuarially sound reserves, notify participants if the plan is self‑funded, and file quarterly and annual reports with the Department (Department of Labor). Reports must include financials, an actuary’s adequacy statement, evidence of stop‑loss coverage from an insurer licensed in Nebraska naming the PEO as insured (with 30‑day termination notice to the PEO and the Commissioner of Labor), and a compliance certificate. The Department may hold compliance hearings, issue orders to comply, and revoke a PEO’s registration for noncompliance. The bill also treats PEOs as employers for sponsoring retirement/welfare plans and exempts single‑PEO plans from MEWA registration. No funding or appropriations are included. Adds enforcement and reporting duties for the state "department" (the agency overseeing PEO registration) and references the Commissioner of Labor. PEO-offered health plans may be fully insured or, if self-funded, must use a licensed TPA, hold assets in an ERISA-style trust, maintain actuarially determined reserves, notify participants that the plan is self-funded, and file quarterly plus an annual report with the department within 90 days of plan fiscal year-end. Annual reports must include a financial statement, an actuary's sufficiency statement, confirmation of stop‑loss insurance (issued by a state‑licensed insurer that must give the PEO and the Commissioner of Labor 30 days' written notice before termination), and a compliance certificate. The department may hold hearings (30 days' notice), issue compliance orders (to be met within 30 days), and revoke PEO registration under the Professional Employer Organization Registration Act for failure to comply. 109-1-LB29_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB29_Intro_Copy.docx LB29 requires state agencies subject to the Administrative Procedure Act to review all existing and pending rules beginning January 1, 2026, and every three years thereafter. Summary of added provisions (focus on listed agencies):\n\n- Department of Administrative Services: must prescribe an attestation format for applicants seeking the specified public benefits; applicants must attest they are an "eligible alien" employed as or training to become a law enforcement officer.\n\n- Department of Labor: extends Employment Security Law (unemployment) benefits to eligible aliens employed as or training to become law enforcement officers.\n\n- Department of Correctional Services: eligible aliens employed as, or training to become, law enforcement officers (which would include applicable correctional officers) are explicitly entitled to employment-related public benefits — retirement (County Employees, Nebraska State Patrol, Police Officers, State Employees Retirement Acts), deferred compensation, scholarships/financial aid (including First Responder Recruitment and Retention Act), and other employment-related benefits. Family/dependents are likewise eligible regardless of lawful presence.\n\n- Department of Revenue: no substantive changes, funding, or appropriations affecting Revenue are included.\n\nNo funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified. The section is enacted under 8 U.S.C. 1621(d). DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB302_Final Final Reading Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB302_Final_Copy.docx LB302 repeals observance of daylight saving time in Nebraska, making the State exempt from 15 U.S.C. 260a(a), but that change only becomes operative Jan. 1 after Iowa, Kansas, South Dakota, and Wyoming enact similar laws. The bill amends election law polling hours by time zone and harmonizes statutory time references by fixing sick- and vacation-leave account balancing at 11:59 p.m. central time on Dec. 31. Agencies and officials referenced: Governor (authority to extend leave in hardship cases), the Legislature/Legislative Council and its Executive Board (leave discretion for legislative employees), the Director of Personnel (rulemaking authority), employing state agencies (leave administration and cash-payment obligations), and the Public Employees Retirement Board (treatment of cash payments for certain retirement plan types). No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. Added language makes Nebraska’s standard time follow the Uniform Time Act of 1966 but exempts the state from observing daylight saving time and from 15 U.S.C. 260a(a). The exemption becomes effective January 1 after Iowa, Kansas, South Dakota, and Wyoming each pass similar laws. The provision also states it becomes null and void when subsection (2) of section 49-1301 becomes operative. 109-1-LB304_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB304_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Health and Human Services The bill designates the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) to administer the state's social services program and to participate in federal child care assistance and Child Care Subsidy programs, including adopting payment rates and promulgating related rules. DHHS is required to collaborate with a private nonprofit for an independent evaluation of the 2021 income-eligibility changes if private funding is provided. Funding provisions: Child Care and Development Block Grant (CCDBG) funds must cover state costs from the 2021 eligibility changes; if CCDBG funds are insufficient, Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) funds may be used; no General Funds may be used for those costs except administration. 109-1-LB305_Intro General File Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB305_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Revenue The bill places administration of the new Preceptorship Tax Credit Act with the Department of Revenue. The department must verify applications (including an affidavit), determine completeness, approve and certify credit amounts to qualifying licensed physicians, and may adopt rules to implement the Act. The department may approve up to $1,000,000 in credits per fiscal year, with priority for rural preceptors; once the annual limit is reached no further credits are allowed and same‑day requests are prorated. The bill also amends section 77-2715.07 to list the Preceptorship Tax Credit Act among income tax credits and retains Department of Revenue authority to recapture a separate home‑purchase credit if residency requirements are not met. Department of Revenue responsibilities: require an affidavit and any other documentation the department prescribes to verify an unpaid physician preceptor meets Preceptorship Tax Credit Act criteria; review, approve, and certify qualifying applications; adopt rules to administer the program. Fiscal limits and rules: the department may approve up to $1,000,000 in tax credits per fiscal year, give approval priority to physicians who precepted in rural locations, prorate credits among requests received on the day the annual cap is exceeded, and prohibit transfer/sale of credits. The bill adds this tax credit to the department’s list of credits. No direct appropriations or new budget allocations for the department are specified. DOCX | PDF

109-1-LB308_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB308_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Labor - Defines "Department" as the Department of Labor and "Commissioner" as the Commissioner of Labor. \n- Requires health care staffing agencies to register annually with the Department of Labor and certify certain conditions. \n- Imposes an annual registration fee of $1,500 per Nebraska location (or one $1,500 statewide fee for technology platforms without a physical Nebraska location) payable to the Department. \n- Grants the Commissioner authority to receive and investigate public complaints, conduct investigations and random audits, administer oaths, issue and enforce subpoenas, and pursue enforcement actions (with legal representation by Department attorneys or the Attorney General). \n- Directs the Department to create and publish a public database of registered agencies and authorizes the Department to adopt rules and regulations. \n- Adds the Health Care Staffing Agency Registration Act to the Department’s administrative duties. Operative January 1, 2026. Summary (Department of Labor focus):\n\n- Establishes the Commissioner of Labor and the Department of Labor as the registering authority for health care staffing agencies under the new Health Care Staffing Agency Registration Act. \n- Agencies must annually register with the Department and certify they will not enforce pre‑registration noncompete clauses. \n- Annual registration fee: $1,500 per separate Nebraska location (health care technology platforms without a Nebraska physical location pay $1,500 for a statewide application). Renewal applications due ≥60 days before expiration; appeals of citations to the Commissioner within 20 days. \n- Department duties: create a public complaint system, investigate complaints, conduct random audits (≥3 business days’ notice), subpoena and compel documents/witnesses, and maintain a public online registration database (including approval and expiration/revocation dates). \n- Department may promulgate rules; legal representation provided by departmental attorneys or Attorney General. \n- No other appropriations or budget allocations specified. 109-1-LB309_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB309_Intro_Copy.docx LB309 (2025) creates the Safe Battery Collection and Recycling Act and delegates administration to the Nebraska Department of Environment and Energy ("department"). Key agency actions: review and approve battery stewardship plans (120-day review clock), require periodic plan updates, audit plans after five years, host approved plans and annual reports on the department website (with proprietary exemptions), review out-of-state studies and report to the Legislature's Natural Resources Committee by May 30, 2028, and adopt implementing rules. Enforcement authorities: Attorney General and county attorneys may seek injunctions; civil penalties remit to the State Treasurer. Fiscal provisions: establishes the Battery Stewardship Cash Fund, consisting of fees collected under section 4, administered by the department and restricted to implementing the Act; funds may be invested by the State Investment Officer under existing state investment law. Creates the Department of Environment and Energy as the lead agency to administer the Safe Battery Collection and Recycling Act: approving and reviewing battery stewardship plans (plans due Jan 1, 2027; department must act within 120 days), posting approved plans and annual reports on its website, reviewing out‑of‑state studies and reporting to the Legislature (Natural Resources Committee by May 30, 2028), and adopting rules. Establishes the Battery Stewardship Cash Fund, funded by fees under section 4, administered by the department and invested by the state investment officer under state investment laws; monies may be used only to carry out the Act. Civil penalties are remitted to the State Treasurer; Attorney General and county attorneys may enforce. DOCX | PDF
109-1-LB30_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB30_Intro_Copy.docx LB30 amends Nebraska's income tax statute (section 77-2716) to allow individuals to subtract from federal adjusted gross income amounts received as overtime compensation paid pursuant to the federal Fair Labor Standards Act (effective taxable years beginning on or after Jan. 1, 2025). The change will be implemented by the Nebraska Department of Revenue/Tax Commissioner in administering section 77-2716. The bill text references multiple programs and agencies elsewhere in the statute, including the Nebraska educational savings plan trust, the ABLE program, the Nebraska National Guard, the Medical Debt Relief Fund, the Teach in Nebraska Today Act, Segal AmeriCorps awards, the U.S. Department of Defense, and the U.S. Office of Personnel Management. No appropriations or budget changes are included. Effective for taxable years beginning (or deemed to begin) on or after Jan. 1, 2025, individuals may subtract from their federal adjusted gross income any overtime pay they received under the federal Fair Labor Standards Act, to the extent that pay is included in federal AGI. The provision cites the Internal Revenue Code and the FLSA (federal statutes); no specific federal agencies, departments, or any funding, appropriation, or budget allocations are mentioned. 109-1-LB310_Intro Referral Legislature 109, Session 1 (2025) 109 1 LB310_Intro_Copy.docx Department of Health and Human Services LB310 amends §71-519 to (1) confirm that the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) may specify additional newborn screening conditions and designate the laboratory, collection, submission, timing, and reporting requirements for screening and confirmatory testing; (2) require hospitals/birthing facilities to provide infant/maternal contact and care information to DHHS on request for tracking, monitoring, and referral; (3) vest DHHS with authority over use, retention, and disposal of residual newborn blood specimens, including rulemaking (consistent with federal law and accreditation), witness-verified disposal records, and limits on research use for public health purposes; and (4) authorize DHHS to charge reasonable fees for evaluating and supplying specimens for approved research and to prepare explanatory written materials. No funding or appropriation changes are included. Adds a parental‑consent exemption: DHHS may not require an infant to undergo the subsection (1) screening if the infant’s parent or guardian objects.
